lead.label: Civic space · Cyber law
lead.headline: Cyber law draft halves rumour penalty; public comments due 25 Nov
lead.summary: The revised Cyber Security (Amendment) Act draft cuts the rumour penalty to five years, but agencies could still block content without a court. NGOs and rights groups can comment until 25 November.

alsoToday.label: Humanitarian · Rohingya response
alsoToday.headline: Rohingya food aid funded only to April 2027, commissioner warns
alsoToday.summary: Most refugees now get $7 to $10 a month for food instead of $12, and acute malnutrition among young Rohingya children has risen to 14.6%.

special.headline: Aid cuts are pushing Bangladesh's NGOs from services to lending
special.summary: A BIDS study finds 2,170 NGOs have no lending income, and many are cutting services first and turning into lenders.

spotlight.label: Spotlight
spotlight.title: COP31 in Antalya
spotlight.intro: Bangladesh wants adaptation finance tripled and paid as grants, not loans, plus real money for loss and damage. Devlens follows what the summit means for the sector until the talks close.

today.text: The talks reached their halfway point with the 1.5C goal as the main fight. Australia, which chairs the talks, has released a summary of positions: some countries want the final deal to say 1.5C remains the goal, while observers say the Arab Group and the Like-Minded Developing Countries may try to drop it. Some developing countries worry that a stronger 1.5C line would mean more pressure to cut emissions without more finance. Bangladesh's delegation is pressing for grant-based adaptation money; its adaptation need is about $8.5 billion a year, with under $0.5 billion coming from abroad.

watch: Adaptation finance: whether a draft text sets a baseline or share for adaptation money, after Bangladesh asked for at least 50%.
Just transition: whether the Belém-Antalya Action Mechanism is adopted.
Finance on the agenda: developing countries want tripling adaptation finance discussed; developed countries are resisting, and an EU official has warned of no political will for new pledges.
Gender: UN Women found 73% of countries recognise gender-specific climate risks, but just over one in three address them fully.
